units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I did my walk, like I promised. 20:40, lights on between 6 and 8, same trainers, left hand on rail, phone in right, Tobin's recorder taped to rail on 7 like Hollis said. Clap at 8, clap at 6. I counted 38 in my head. Tobin says the file also has 38. So with lights on, I am normal. Good. But then I ask, why 43 that night. Same man, same shoes.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Results, controlled walk 2. 1. Walker: Benedikt. 2. Events between claps: 38. 3. Extra events: 0. 4. Mean interval 0.61 s, slower than Jordie (0.55 s), as expected for a man after a twelve-hour shift. So two clean baselines. The variable we have not controlled is the lights. Every recording with extras was made with the 6-8 lights out. That is the next test, not a theory.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Careful. The lights aren't the only thing that differs. The original was after 01:00, with the building asleep, the lift locked off and the heating cycling. Tonight was 20:40 with televisions on every floor. A quiet building lets you hear sources you'd normally miss, footfall on another core included. If you test 'lights off' at 21:00 you'll learn about 21:00, not about the lights.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Agreed, which is why the test should be at 01:30 with the lights off, as on the night. The relay has been failing on its own most nights. If it does not fail, the circuit breaker for the 6-8 riser is in the cupboard on 7 and I know which one it is. I am a signalling technician. Isolating a lighting circuit for ten minutes is not difficult.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: tobin mate i will walk the stairs in the dark for science but i'm not being an accessory to you breaking into the riser cupboard. kerrow put that 'do not tamper' line in the notice for a reason and the reason is probably you. we just wait for a night it goes off on its own, which is like every night

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Tobin, please no cupboard. If Kerrow say we break something they will not fix anything and blame us forever. I am happy to walk again when lights fail by themselves. I finish at 22:00 most days this week. After storm maybe.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (Fourteen, working on the cereal mascot, who is a badger in a scarf, don't ask.) For the log, since we're logging: 02:50, three steps on the riser stairs below me, going up, unhurried, then nothing. The roof door didn't open, I'd have heard the bar. I didn't look. I'm writing it down because Tobin says that's what counts, not because I think it's anything.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ivy that was probably me, i went up to 13 at about ten to three to give marco his charger back. i walk like a man who is unhurried because i am always unhurried. sorry if i ruined the badger

units.author: dc_14_ivy

edit.note: edited: added the bit about the lift
edit.text: (Ah. That's one mystery solved and a gold star for Jordie.) Mystery reclassified as 'a student with a charger'. The badger survives. Though to be fair to my ears, I heard the steps go up past 13 and keep going for a flight, and Marco is on 13. Added later: Jordie says he took the lift back down, which would explain why I didn't hear him come down. Fine. Filed.

units.text: (Ah. That's one mystery solved and a gold star for Jordie.) Mystery reclassified as 'a student with a charger'. The badger survives. Though to be fair to my ears, I heard the steps go up past 13 and keep going for a flight, and Marco is on 13. I'll ask him in the morning if anyone else came up.

units.title: Housing transfers: has anyone actually done one?
units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Sorry, practical question, not about the stairs. Has anyone here applied for a transfer, either through Kerrow's own list or the council's? Two bedrooms, ground or first floor ideally, Weyhaven or Tollinby, my mum is in Tollinby. R. stops at the 6 landing every evening now and little M. copies him because he copies everything. I'd just like to know how long it really takes before I start hoping.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Soraya, the council list is the one that moves. Kerrow's internal list hasn't moved since they replaced the lift motor, and that was three years ago. Bring your tenancy letter and the kids' school letters to the next meeting and I'll photocopy the forms at work for free. Being near family counts for points, so put your mum's address on it. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Soraya, my cousin went from the Quay blocks to Tollinby in seven months on the council list. Medical points helped, the doctor wrote about her boy's asthma. If the kids aren't sleeping, ask the GP to write that too, it counts. Meanwhile I have a box of plug-in nightlights at the shop, take two for the kids' room, no charge. H

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Thank you both, honestly. I'll ring the GP in the morning and come to the meeting with a folder like a proper grown-up. Hassan, I'll pick up the nightlights when I do the milk and I'm paying for one at least, don't argue. R. wants the one shaped like a moon. M. wants whatever R. wants.

units.title: The torch on the 7th floor landing
units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, Thank you to whoever hung the torch on a string on the 7th floor landing rail. It is a good torch. I used it at six this morning when the lights were out again between 6 and 8, and I want to report that I heard nothing at all, so that you have both kinds of news. My husband would have said the string was not strong enough. I have replaced it with button thread. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Irena, the torch was me. The string was from the bread deliveries, so you are right, it was not strong. Thank you for the button thread. The batteries are new and I'll check them every week when I do the shop stock. If anyone wants one for 6 or 8 too, tell me. H

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: irena reporting that she heard nothing is the most reassuring post this board has ever had. a torch on button thread. i love this building. hassan put me down for one on 6, the cardio of doom now has mood lighting

units.title: East side bins (again) and the lift before the storm
units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: The east side bins have not been emptied since the private firm came at five in the morning last week and took one in three. They are now overflowing onto the path and the gulls have found them. The storm tomorrow will finish the job. Also, I am told the lift will be switched off in high winds 'as a precaution'. Can someone tell me how a lift inside a concrete building knows it is windy?

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: wendell actual engineering answer: the lift shaft moves a bit when the building sways in big gusts and the ropes can swing, so the controller has a wind sensor on the roof. not a joke. the lift does know. i'm as surprised as you

units.author: dc_12_ollie
units.text: my mum says the gulls got into the bins and one of them took a whole pizza box onto the car roof of the man from 5. it was there when we came home from school. is the lift going off tomorow for definite because i have football

units.title: Group session: plan, positions and rules (first calm night after the storm)
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Since a few of you asked: the group session goes ahead on the first calm night after this storm, then as many nights as the weather and Mr Ashcombe allow. Positions: me at the dam path with two omnis and the dish, tern at the pumping house, Odile with the binaural head on the reservoir road halfway between. Clocks from GPS loggers, claps called by voice at start and end. Road only, off by four. Raw files to the shared folder. Make of it what you will.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Also: tern's GPS logger arrived, so tonight the two of us are doing a ninety-minute kit test before the wind gets up, 22:40 to about 00:10. Me at the dam path, him at the pumping house. This is not the session and nobody else needs to come out. It's to check the loggers and the sync sheet, nothing more.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for this one, eventually! Gerald (the binaural head, he has a name now, the radiography lot insisted) is packed in his foam box. I'm on call tonight and tomorrow, so the first calm night suits me better anyway. tern, I'll bring him over to yours before the session so you can try the levels. Please nobody sit on him.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so at the pumping house, H5 on the wall bracket facing the trees, logger in my coat. synced 22:31:00 off the logger and said it out loud twice so hollis can't say anything. levels -18 on my own clap. it is very dark and there's a sheep in the field behind the fence that is going to be on every single file

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Pinning this. Housekeeping for the session: check-ins and timestamps in this thread while you're out, discussion afterwards. Raw files only in the shared folder, not phone recordings of your speakers. Nobody tags along uninvited, and nothing gets streamed. Thanks dunlin for doing it properly.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: guys is the test open?? i can be at brackwater in 40 mins with the IR cam and the shotgun mic, we could go live from the pumping house before the storm hits, the wind would make it even better honestly. this is literally the content

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: no. please don't. it's a battery test in a field. the most exciting thing that's going to happen is the sheep

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: It's closed, by invitation of the organiser, as the pinned rules say. And the estate is shut after dusk; the ranger has been clear about that. Please don't turn up.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Gilliver: wind already backing south, swell running up the slip. Note for your files tonight, if you hear a low boom around midnight it's not the woods, it's sound carrying from the water company's pumping station on the ridge, which starts at 00:00 on cheap power. Sound travels oddly ahead of a front.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: 00:30, packed up. Test result: both loggers agree within 40 ms over 90 minutes, which is what they're for. Content: owls, one fox, a car on the reservoir road at 00:10 with its stereo up, wind starting in the tops by 23:50. Two faint impacts on the dish around 23:53, bearing roughly east, could easily be a gate. Tern?

units.author: tern_audio

edit.text: ok so I have something at 23:53 too, two dull hits, quite close together. my levels were low so it's barely above the sheep. not claiming anything. I'll look at it properly on the big screen at school when I've slept. the loggers are brilliant though, best £19 I ever spent

units.text: ok so I have something at 23:35 too, two dull hits, quite close together. my levels were low so it's barely above the sheep. not claiming anything. I'll look at it properly on the big screen at school when I've slept. the loggers are brilliant though, best £19 I ever spent

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Good plan, and thank you for putting the logger method first. One request for the real session: log the reservoir valve schedule alongside your files. The outflow valve operates on a timer, usually on the hour, and if any of your impacts land within a few seconds of a valve change, that's the first thing I'll ask about.

units.title: Brackwater estate: access during the storm
units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: For the recordists. The estate gate is locked at 20:00 and stays locked, storm or not. From tomorrow nobody goes in the woods at all, day or night, until I've walked them. Trees come down after a blow, not just during. Use the lay-by on the reservoir road, keep to the road, and if I find anyone in the pheasant pens there'll be words. Mr Dunlin has asked properly, which is more than most.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thank you, Mr Ashcombe. Lay-by, road only, nowhere near the pens, and nobody goes in until you've walked them after the storm. I'll pass your number round the group in case anyone needs it, with strict instructions that nobody rings it for fun.

units.title: Before the storm: keeping old tapes dry
units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: A practical note, since several of you have old cassettes and reels in lofts and garages. Damp is the enemy of tape. Before a wet spell, bring them indoors to a cupboard on an inside wall, upright like books, not flat. Do not put them by a radiator. And if a box smells of vinegar, keep it apart from the others and tell me. Regards, Ned

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Seconded from the catalogue side. We lost most of a 1980s Gilliver harbour cassette to a damp garage two winters ago: the oxide came off on the heads like brown dust. If anyone is holding Brackwater tapes from the 1980s or 90s, the catalogue gap is still there, and I'd far rather digitise them before the storm than after it.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: My uncle's walkman tapes came down from the loft today, eleven of them, labelled in pencil. Two say 'reservoir, dawn'. They're on my kitchen table in a shoebox, upright, as instructed. Ned, would you look at them before anyone plays them?

units.title: Last hydrophone drop before the gale
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Pulled both hydrophones off Bram's mooring this afternoon before it blows. Last night's file, 6 m element: prop wash at 21:10 from the Lisle boat, a pump cycling on the fish-shed outflow every 14 minutes, hull slap, and a lot of shingle moving in the swell, which sounds like rain on a tin roof underwater. It's a pump. It's always a pump.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: A fourteen-minute cycle is textbook float-switch behaviour on a sump pump. Agreed, pump. The shingle is lovely, though. Worth a catalogue entry on its own as a baseline for what a beach does in a swell.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so every recording on this forum should come with a marlo attached. 'it's a pump' saves me a week of squinting at spectrograms. the shingle one is going in my lesson on frequency for year 8, they'll think it's rain and then I'll tell them it's rocks

units.title: Courier piece on the Holm clearance (today's paper).
units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Nell Ashdown's piece is in today's Courier, page five and online. It is careful. It quotes the consent conditions correctly, including the one requiring the works to finish within the approved period, which is more than this board managed last week. There is nothing in it that isn't on the planning portal, apart from Ardent Vale's statement, which says nothing in three sentences.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Thank you. A reminder for this thread: the article names two companies, Grieve Land Services and Ardent Vale Holdings. It does not name anyone working on the Holm, and nor shall we. Posts guessing at who is on the crew, or where their families live, will be removed without discussion. Pell (Admin).

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see if this were ordinary land speculation? A clearance ahead of a resale or a change of use, a buyer who keeps quiet so the price doesn't move, and a contractor on a deadline because the buyer's money is borrowed and expensive. That is very nearly what the article describes. The quiet is the least surprising part.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Notice that she asks Ardent Vale three straight questions and gets back three sentences about 'stewardship'. Three. Sentences. I'm just asking questions here, but when one of the richest private companies around won't say what it's building on an island it's paying to strip bare in thirty days, people are entitled to wonder. Do your research.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Gil, the article doesn't say Ardent Vale is building anything. It says they haven't said what they intend. Those are different sentences, and only one of them is in the paper.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I was pleased to see Ms Ashdown describe the curing station correctly, as a curing station. Somebody at the Courier has been reading the right books. On that subject, I have found my class's 1991 project on the Holm in the loft, and I shall put a short summary in Local Oddities this morning for those who asked.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: For background, the Society's pages on the curing station and the 1890s timber camp are both linked from the article's online version, which was kind of them. Please read the talk pages before quoting either as fact. The camp page in particular has two editors and roughly three opinions.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: page five for 'company cuts down trees'. slow week at the Courier. next week: man mows lawn, neighbours demand answers

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 5, offered calmly: the piece says the Holm was bought 'through an intermediary', which matches what I posted earlier this month, and I'm glad to see it in print. It doesn't name the intermediary. I won't either, but I will repeat that a nominee buyer is ordinary for a purchase of this size. That is what nominee companies are for, and it tells us nothing about the use.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: The piece says the boats go out at first light and come back before dark, and that is quite right, you could set the clock by them from my front room. I was the retired shopkeeper, though I was never a shopkeeper, I was the post office counter. I didnt mind. She was a nice girl and she wrote down exactly what I said about the clock.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Fair play to the Courier. For the record, if Grieve read this, I'm still available for subcontract on the Holm or anywhere else, CS30, CS31, own saw, own boots, own lunch. Thirty days for that many trees, they'll want help by the end, mark my words. Port ammet based, will travel.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Davey, Trades & Jobs please, where your own thread is still open. I shall leave this one here, as it is at least on the subject. Pell (Admin).

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Agreed, and thank you for saying the second half out loud. For anyone reading the planning file for the first time tonight: 'total vegetation clearance' is a description of works, not of a use. There is no change-of-use application for the Holm on the portal. If one appears, I will post it here the same evening.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: No change-of-use application YET. Has anyone asked about the boats? Who goes out there and when? Bram, you're on the water, what goes across at night?

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Nothing goes across at night. Not ours. The supply boat goes out in daylight and comes back in daylight, like any sensible boat. Aye, and it'll not go at all tomorrow, nor will I.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Read the article twice. Note what isn't in it... a thirty day deadline for an island nobody lives on. Ask yourself who needs it finished by then, and why. I'm not saying any more than that. I've already said more than I should.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: 'Who needs it finished by then' is answered in paragraph four. The contract does. That's what contracts are. Source? Read it.

units.title: Lisle School, 1991: 'The Holm in Our Grandparents' Time'. A summary.
units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: For those who asked. In 1991 my class of twenty-six interviewed their grandparents about the Holm. The curing station ran from about 1880 to 1931: two salting sheds, a cooperage, a stone jetty. Nobody ill was ever sent there. Three grandparents spoke of the 1890s timber camp. Two said it was given up over wages. One said it was given up 'for the dark', and would not explain. I have kept the children's spelling in my notes.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Thank you, Mrs Hale. With your permission I'd like to add the project to the Society's holdings. The 'wages' versus 'the dark' split matches the 1976 oral history very closely, which means either both are right, or the 1991 grandparents were repeating what their own neighbours told the 1976 interviewers. Citation needed, as ever.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Of course you may. I shall bring the folder to the Society on the first fine day. And please stop writing 'citation needed' after your own sentences; I taught you to spell 'necessary' and I can still see you sitting by the radiator not doing it.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I remember those children coming over on the boat with their clipboards. One little boy asked me if the Holm was haunted and I told him no, it was only empty. He wrote down 'only empty' very carefully and underlined it twice. I hope he is well, whoever he was.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: I was in that class. I interviewed my grandad, who talked about herring prices for forty minutes and then fell asleep. The 'for the dark' one was Susie Dray's nan, I think, and in fairness Susie's nan said a lot of things, including that the ferry was run by Methodists. Good to see the project survived, Mrs Hale.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Ewan, the ferry was run by a Methodist, which is not the same thing, and your grandfather's herring prices are on page four, every one of them. I gave you a merit for persistence.

units.title: Day 13 readings: here it comes
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 06:30, Carrow Point: 996.2 hPa and falling 2.4 in three hours. Wind S 14 knots gusting 24. Air 11.8 C, dew point 11.1 C, so still very mild and very wet-feeling. Visibility 8 km in drizzle. The Met Office have a yellow warning from this evening and are being polite about tomorrow. I'm less polite. Tie down your bins and apologise to the gulls.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Practical questions from the school-gate front: 1. Does Tollinby Primary close for an amber warning or only red? 2. If the power goes, how long can a chest freezer stay shut before I panic? (I know Garvey answered this once, I've lost the post.) 3. Is it just our shop on Market Street that's run out of bread already, or everywhere?

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: 2: a full chest freezer is fine 24 to 48 hrs if you don't open it. 3: everywhere, I did the Tollinby drop at 16:00 and the bread shelves were bare at both ends. Bonus: the Tollinby rd floods at the dip by the garden centre every big blow, go round by the B-road even though the Brackwater jct lights are still stuck on red. Of course they are.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Ferry app now says 'at risk' for tomorrow, which in my long experience means 'no'. Office says 'work from home if you can safely do so', which means my manager, who lives above the office, will be the only one in and will email us all at 07:01 to say so.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: We have paraffin in for the lamp and a second lamp on the stairs. My nephew has tied the dustbin to the drainpipe with the rope he uses for the boat, which I think is too much rope for a dustbin, but he says the last time it went over the wall into the harbour and he had to pay for a new one.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Free tip from a man who'll be up trees all weekend: if you've got a big tree near the house, move the car away from it tonight, not tomorrow morning. And fill a can of petrol for the generator now while the pumps still work. Chainsaw call-outs after the storm, insured, sensible rates, number in my Trades post.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00: 988.0 hPa, eight down since breakfast. Gusting 38 knots at the station already. Rain rate picking up. The Met's amber is from 06:00 tomorrow; on these numbers I'd have started it at midnight, but they have more computers than I do. I have put the garden chairs in the shed and the anemometer is on its own.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: every year. 'the storm of the century'. it'll be a bit windy, a fence will fall over and somebody's trampoline will end up in Lisle. the bread panic is the only real disaster

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Cal, I sold a book this afternoon to a man who was buying it 'in case the power goes'. Six hundred pages, about a whaling voyage. I didn't have the heart to tell him that if the power goes for long enough to finish it, the bread will be the least of his worries. Goodnight, all. Tie your gates.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: An update for the record. Numbers 23 to 40 Rope Walk remain uncollected after the van's partial visit. The council's own newsletter says the replacement lorry is 'awaiting a part'. I telephoned. The part is a gearbox. There is a storm tomorrow, and the council has suspended collections, so I shall now be storing three weeks of recycling and a storm's worth of cardboard in my hallway. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Same here in Weyhaven, Bernard. Our landlord pays a private firm that came at five in the morning last week, took one bin in three and left. I rang the number on the side of the lorry. It is a fax number. I did not know fax numbers still existed. Neither, I think, does the firm.

units.title: Last night's crossings, and the plan for the blow
units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Last night's crossings ran within six minutes of time. Swell building at the Lisle approach by the 00:55. Gilliver slip clear on both visits; the chain was on. For the storm: Sound Lines will decide tomorrow's sailings at 06:00 off the inshore forecast, but I'd expect nothing to run from early morning. We'll take her round to the lee berth at Port Ammet after tonight's last run. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: For anyone wondering, yes, I'm on tonight, and no, I don't want to hear one more heron noise from the deck. Colin is a heron. Everybody knows Colin is a heron. What I logged on the fifth wasn't Colin, and I'm done explaining the difference to grown men making beak shapes with their hands at the rail.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: that was me doing the beak, sorry kerris. in my defence it was a very good beak. but fine, no more colin. also can we log that the tea in the 23:40 urn is now officially a hazard, it's been stewing since the 20:15 and it tastes like the inside of a boot

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: fair enough kerris. lads, give it a rest on here and on the boat. anyone wants to do heron impressions can take it to the sound board. finn, tea urn descaler is on the shelf behind the counter, no charge, for the good of the service

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: I'm with Kerris on the not laughing. Mine at Lisle might still have been an angler... ha, anyway. If it was, he's the quietest angler on Lisle and he didn't leave a bucket or a single bit of line. I've stopped telling people about it on the boat, they just look at me.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: no heron noises. understood. what about owl noises. asking because there's going to be no ferry tomorrow and i'll have loads of time to practise

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: right lads, storm proper tomorrow. double your lines on the inner pontoon, it's not optional, the HM will say the same. 16 mm three strand at last week's price till it's gone, fenders too. anyone needs a hand hauling punts up above the tide line shout before dark today, me and the van are about till six

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Harbour Notice 13/1. Under Harbour Byelaw 6, owners of vessels on the inner moorings are asked to double all mooring lines, fit chafe protection and remove loose gear from decks before 18:00 today. The slipway will be closed to launching and recovery from 06:00 tomorrow until further notice. Thank you, and please look after each other. HM Quill

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Engine room has the storm checklist out. Both gensets serviced, fuel polished, bilge alarms tested twice because the first time I didn't believe them. She's a good boat in weather. She just isn't a fast one in weather, which is why she'll be tied up in the lee instead of proving it.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: does anyone know if we get paid standby if the boat doesn't sail. asking for a deckhand who has a phone bill and a very expensive taste in chips

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Lifted the last of the Holm side string this morning, fifty-two pots, three gone to the tide. They're stacked behind the shed and roped. Not putting them back till it's blown through. Brown crab was 3.20 at Ammet, poor, so no great loss to stop.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Linesmen on standby from tonight, all leave cancelled, flaming marvellous. If your power goes tomorrow, don't ring the yard asking for me by name, ring the outage line, it's the same queue and the girl on the phones is nicer than me. And stay well back from anything down. It's not dead just because it's lying on the ground.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: First storm standby for me. Garvey says sleep in my kit and eat now, because I won't later. I've got his list of every pole on the Brackwater ridge in a plastic sleeve. If anyone in Brackwater sees blue flashes on the hill line tomorrow night, that's a fuse going, please report it with where you are, don't film it for the internet.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Finn, it's in your contract, shore standby is paid at the standby rate. Your contract is in the drawer under the chart table with the biscuits, which is why you've never found it.

units.title: The idling van has a name now (and a pillow)
units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Mystery mostly solved. The white van that idles outside the bakery for hours: tonight at one it was there again, so I went out with a tray of seconds. Knocked on the window. A man sat up from across the front seats like a jack-in-the-box. Agency driver. The depot won't let him in before six, so he sleeps between drops with the engine on for the heater. He chose the cinnamon knot.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Logged: vehicle, occupant asleep, resolved. Good result. Did he say why he parks with no lights at all? We get a few like that on the port road and I always have to go and look.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Battery, he said: lights off saves the battery while the heater runs. I didn't follow the logic and I don't think he did either, but he was very sure. He's coming back tomorrow for a proper loaf and has promised to wave so I don't have to knock.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: This is my favourite kind of ending. A body across the front seats, a heater, and a man who has slept in a lot of cold vans. Most of what we see at three in the morning has a tired, ordinary person inside it. Not all of it, perhaps. But most.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Wish mine had ended like that. The van at the retail park, I walked right round it with the torch and the cab was empty, seats and all, I'd swear to that in front of Control. But congratulations, honestly. That's excellent bun diplomacy.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: marking this one resolved, with thanks. A gentle reminder that knocking on a stranger's van window at one in the morning is your own call and not a forum recommendation. The cinnamon knot, however, is.

units.title: update: the corridor lights
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: facilities came!! the motion sensor at the stairwell end of my corridor was faulty, the guy showed me: it was triggering off the heating vent above it. warm air drifting across the corridor = 'person walking'. he swapped it while I watched. very undramatic. so for about a week I was being visited by a radiator. chapter 3 is still due. I have eaten nothing but crisps for four days.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: 'Visited by a radiator' is the best sentence I've read this year. Come in tonight. The rice balls are on offer and I'll pretend not to notice if you buy six.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Heating-vent triggers on passive infrared sensors are common and underrated. A plume of warm air moving across a cold corridor looks to the sensor exactly like a slow walker. Lovely, tidy result. Please eat a vegetable.

units.title: All-night coffee on the Flats run, ranked, plus one stretch you should do
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: For the newer folks. Best coffee: the stop at the grain elevator junction, they brew fresh at two sharp. Worst: the place with the pie case by the scales, don't. Every two hours, get out, walk round the rig twice and touch all the lights. Sounds daft. It keeps you honest about how awake you really are, and it's how I caught a dead marker light last week.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Seconding the walk-round. I do a full round of the kennels at the top of every hour, even when they're all asleep, for the same reason: it tells me I'm awake, not them. Biscuit (collie cross, very opinionated) now walks it with me and checks every door like she's the night manager.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Update on the back corridor, since a few asked: the vent's clean, the mouse is long gone, the smell's gone. Rufus still sits down at the corner and won't go on. I'm not making anything of it. He's eleven and he's allowed his opinions. I take him round the front way and he's perfectly happy.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Old dogs know things, Jo. Mostly where the biscuits are kept and which floor's coldest. Give Rufus a scratch from a stranger. I'll be through your town Thursday week if the weather holds.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: touch all the lights is good advice for taxis too except I've only got four and one of the back ones has been out since summer and the inspector keeps not noticing, anyway the best coffee in Halvard is the hospital rank machine, I will not be taking questions

units.title: Storm countdown at the distribution centre
units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Rate went up to 140 lines an hour tonight because 'everyone's panic buying before the storm'. My scanner says 'too slow' in a voice like a disappointed aunt. The yard's full of trailers that can't leave till it blows through, so all the dock doors are shut and it's like picking inside a fridge. Anyone else on the storm countdown?

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Control has put us on 'storm posture', which means I'm allowed to wear the big coat. They want every trolley bay chained by 02:00 tomorrow so the wind doesn't send them through the shop windows. I've seen it happen once. They go across the car park like a flock of metal geese.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: We've been told to stock the trolleys 'like it's a bank holiday'. A&E have already had one man who tried to take his trampoline down early and dropped it on his own foot. I wheeled him to x-ray. He said it was a pre-emptive injury. Fair.

units.title: A swell from nowhere
units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: The storm you're all talking about is a long way from my light, and yet something of it has arrived: a slow swell from the north-east, out of a sky with no weather in it, lifting the boat at the landing in long breaths. The lens room smells of brass polish and paraffin, though nobody has burnt paraffin here in thirty years. I polished the brass anyway. It seemed polite.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Same underground before a big blow up top. Pressure drops, the ventilation doors pull different, you feel it in your ears on the cage. Old hands say the mountain's listening. It's the fans. Home on the bus now.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: There's a line in an old sea novel I sell too many copies of, about the sea arriving before the news of the weather does. Your swell put me in mind of it. Ours arrives tomorrow, apparently, in person. Goodnight, or good evening, whichever it is at your lamp.

units.title: The 03:17 caller, night six
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Same number, 03:17 my time, sixth night running. Silence, a faint hiss like someone's in a car with the fan on, then it drops at exactly 41 seconds. Every night 41. My supervisor says log it and move on. I log it. I move on. Then I hum the hold music for an hour because it lives in my bones now. (Brb, queue's lit up.)

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Hana: the same minute, the same length to the second, every night. That's a machine. People don't keep time that well, not even the lonely ones, and I get a lot of lonely ones. I'll bet you a studio biscuit it's a dialler somewhere that's lost its list and only knows you.

units.title: Vending machine report, B corridor
units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: The B corridor vending machine has taken its revenge for last winter. It now accepts coins, displays 'thank you', and keeps them. Three of us have fed it tonight. It's the best-paid member of the night shift. Estates say they'll 'look at it after the storm', which is what they said about the lift in the old wing in 2019.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Ours on 9 only gives out tomato soup. Whatever you press. Even if you press 'water'. We've stopped fighting it and now call it the soup machine on the rota. Back to it.
